payload.text: Flattery is charming, señor, but I know every print run in Madrid — all nine of them. My figure does not wander with the afternoon light. 151 P, the same honest sum. Take it, and the album closes beautifully this Sunday.

Ay, hola cariño, come, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look, this one, Té Moruno — a pretty card, my favourite little green one. For you, five P. My grandson started with this very card, you know. He still keeps it, the sentimental boy.

Ay, one thirty-five! Paco, cover your ears — he's a sensitive boy. Jefe, listen: gloves, sealed box, Valencia, and the green coat man already offered more. We like your face, so 151 P and the case closes. Sí? Say it fast, before Nando changes his mind.

Paco: "Forty-six, like a little bell!" Nando: "Ding, ding, hermano." Amigo, the bell doesn't buy cards. Sixty-three primas, La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, wrapped and warm. We've stood here longer for you than for any duquesa. Sí — hand me the cash and smile.
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Señor, numbers do not become clearer by repeating them louder. Mine has not moved since we began: 151 P for La Puerta de Alcalá. Clear, honest, and final in its elegance. Shall we close the album this Sunday?

Paco: "Forty-six, one last ding." Nando: "And we're out of bells, hermano." Amigo, no hard feelings — you're good company, truly. But today we can't go further, so we'll shake your hand and roll the van. Find us next market, eh? Who knows what's in the case then. ¡Adiós, guapo!
Done! 142 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!

"¡Amigo, amigo! Come, come, you have the face of a lucky man today —" "— and lucky men find us first, eh, Paco?" "Nando, show him! Té Moruno, fresh from the caravan, the real thing." "Four pesetas. Four! For you only, and only while the kettle is hot."
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!

Ay, hija, you are too generous with me! No, no — five P, that is the price, and not a céntimo more. Keep your coins for a bocadillo, you look hungry. Take the little green one, enjoy it, and come back next Sunday to tell me.
Then let your heart rest, señor — walk nowhere. The album waits open on my table, and my figure waits too: 151 P. It has not moved, and it will not. Shall we finish this elegantly?

¡Hombre, un lector! Rinconete y Cortadillo, ¡nuestros abuelos! —Nuestros primos, Nando. —Eso. Mira, nada de estampitas: te ponemos El Organillero, pieza fina, suena solo cuando nadie mira. Cuatro primas y te lo llevas. —Cuatro, sí. Rapidito, que el tren no espera.

¡Ay, qué bien, hijo, un cocido con los tres vuelcos! Así da gusto. Pues mira, quince primas por La Ardilla, hecho, trato cerrado. Toma, llévatela con cuidado en la funda.

Y luego pásate por El Chato, el de al lado; abre a las nueve y media esta noche. Le gusta la gente que trata derecho, como tú.

¡Hombre, un paisano con buen gusto! Gallinejas en Cascorro, ¡eso es Madrid puro! —Y caracoles, Paco, no olvides los caracoles. Mira, amigo: La Cebada, joya rara, para ti, ahora mismo, cuatro P. —Cuatro, dice, ¡y se nos va el tren! Dinos que sí y la envolvemos.
Let us be civilised: 151 P. Don Ernesto at Casa Prima only receives the most accomplished collectors. On Sunday.
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more!

"¡Paco, this man bargains like my aunt!" "Amigo, listen — four pesetas. Four. That is the last word from these two mouths, eh, Nando?" "The last! Say no and we take the tea, the suitcase, the taxi, and we are gone. Decide, amigo — ¡ahora!"
Psst. La Heroína del Dos de Mayo. For you only, 73 P.
Señor, we have circled the Puerta long enough. My figure is the same one I gave you first: 151 P. Patience is charming, but it does not change arithmetic. Say yes, and Sunday will be beautiful.

Ay, cariño, qué cabezota eres — but no. Five P, that is my price and I am happy with it. Té Moruno is yours. Keep the rest for something to eat, hija, you look thin. Come Sunday and tell me how you like her.

—¡Ay, el Lazarillo! Buen regateo, pero cuatro primas es cuatro primas, hermano. El Organillero se va contigo ahora mismo.

—Nando, dile lo del coche.

—Eso, que la policí... digo, el taxi nos espera en la esquina con el motor en marcha. ¡Decide ya, que volamos!

¡Oreja, bravas, torreznos! Paco, se me hace la boca agua. —¡Y una limoná, hombre! Pero escucha: La Cebada, cuatro P, ni un céntimo distinto. —¡Rápido, rápido, que el carro arranca y nos vamos en un minuto! Di que sí y brindamos contigo. —Si no, se la lleva otro. ¡Venga, paisano!
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 67 P.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer.

Paco: "Again the same number, hermano!" Nando: "He's testing our hearts." Listen, amigo, this card survived a siege, she's not going for pocket change. Sixty-seven primas, same as before, and we're already weeping. Cash in hand, card in your bag, and we vanish. ¿Sí?
Oh, you're killing us. 67 P.

¡Luis Candelas, dice! Paco, nos halaga y nos aprieta. —¡Max Estrella nos pondría un verso! Pero mira, paisano: cuatro P, La Cebada, y envuelta en papel de seda. —¡Corre, que la policía... digo, el taxi está esperando en la esquina con el motor en marcha! ¡Decide ahora o volamos!

Paco: "Hermano, he's stuck like a wheel in mud!" Nando: "Forty-six, forty-six, the man sings one song." Amigo, we adore you, but La Heroína doesn't move for that. Sixty-seven primas, same as ever, and we throw in a handshake and a story. ¿Trato hecho?

Good evening. El Marqués, 61 P. I trust that suits you. They say only one golden chulapa was ever printed. Carmen at El Rastro knows the story; ask her about the golden chulapa. Don Ernesto at Casa Prima only receives the most accomplished collectors. On Sunday.

Paco: "Nando, he's a broken bell!" Nando: "Ding, ding, forty-six." Amigo, our mother sang better tunes. La Heroína stays sixty-seven primas, not one less. Say the word, the suitcase closes, we're gone before the bells ring. Sixty-seven. ¿Sí o no?
A warm home it would have, yes. But I know exactly what El Marqués is worth, señor, and my figure does not wander. Sixty-one pesetas, the same as before. Shall we close it?

Paco: "Hermano, close the suitcase." Nando: "Already closing." Amigo, we love you, truly, but today our songs don't meet. No hard feelings, none at all — come find us another market day, maybe La Heroína's mood will change. Un abrazo, and good luck out there. We're off!
Señor, we are not haggling in a market stall. My number was precise the first time and remains so: sixty-one pesetas for El Marqués. Say yes, and it joins my Salamanca page on Sunday.
We close at 23:00. Offers stay open; the clock stops.

Ay, hola cariño, come, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? No? Later, later. Look here — Guantería Antigua, this one I keep for someone nice. Twenty-nine P, hijo. My hands have held this card since many Sundays ago. You will like it, I think.
Amigo! Noche de Movida, 73 P, a gift, a real gift! Another team offered us much more just now.
